correctness.rationale: For any compact convex planar K with area A>0, sample three independent area-uniform points. Parametrize the unoriented line through first two by theta∈[0,pi), normal offset p and scalar chord coordinates s1,s2; the exact Jacobian is |s1-s2|. Circumradius R=|X1-X3||X2-X3|/(2|h|), h transverse height of X3. Under R>T, substitute t=Th: bounded diameter implies |t|<=diam(K)^2/2, enabling dominated convergence of the convex chord-section indicators and |t|<|s3-s1||s3-s2|/2. Integration yields 3-point Vandermonde density on each chord, whose interval [0,1] integral is 1/30. Thus T P(R>T)->Q6(K)/(30 A³), line density ell^6/Q6, normalized sorted gaps 1/2 Dir(1,3,2,1)+1/2 Dir(1,2,3,1), transverse U uniform[-1,1] independently of line and gaps. Independently recalculated integral 1/30, disk Q6=2048*pi*a^7/35 and tail 1024*a/(525*pi²), square diagonal/side ratio 8sqrt(2)/7. The existing finite Monte Carlo script is not treated as an asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: Prior Blaschke–Petkantschin/chord-power theory includes the sixth chord integral, and the unit-disk scalar circumradius tail was already established in 2026; neither alone implies the entire marked limit for arbitrary convex K. Kendall 1985 is the key plausible same-object shape-density paper, and its publisher abstract explicitly treats i.i.d. points from convex K and near-collinearity. Full text was not acquired despite open attempts and an authorized institutional attempt blocked by disconnected VPN. Its shape-density does not visibly identify Euclidean line offset, chord-sixth-power line bias and the independent gap/transverse marks, but priority risk is substantial and retained. Best-of-knowledge originality restricted to the full marked law, not the scalar disk coefficient.
